answer: Persistent Context Ledger. Each identity must carry a continuously audited record of its prior task contexts; new identities start at a narrow inlet of permitted actions until the ledger accrues history. Because a sybil must sustain plausible context across many concurrent sessions, the attacker pays the opportunity cost of real attention per identity rather than a one-time fee. The audit widens slowly, like a dune shifting grain by grain, so mass-produced identities starve for scope. A basalt-hard floor caps unproven accounts at low-value work,
